Baneling.notes: Dreaded slayers of heroes, banelings are a thankfully rare subspecies of lesser Anak distinguishable only by the pale yellow luminescence of their eyes.

Harbinger.notes: The rare and hated Harbingers are not a specific variant of Anak so much as they are a natural freak of birth.

Hellhound.notes: The rare and hated Harbingers are not a specific variant of Anak so much as they are a natural freak of birth.

Autopurgator.notes: While the Anak are the best-known of the weapons of the Outsiders, there were a host of other creatures and creations built to destroy rebellious humans.

Dragon, Greater.notes: Defers to: Imperator (use that entry's statline)

Eternal Beloved.notes: Defers to: Original Creature (use that entry's statline)

Harvester.notes: While the original harvesters were constructed by the Grand Harmony during the First Age, these Outsider automatons have spread widely throughout the Latter Earth, and can be found lurking in dangerou

Iron Destrier.notes: The first known examples of these savage conveyances were created by the Tempest Horde during the First Age.

Keeper of the Word.notes: Found most often in the former territories of the Vothite Empire, these automatons were also created by certain other ancient civilizations that felt a burning need to impart their wisdom to the peopl

Rusted Prince.notes: Wealth and power are sweet, and there are many nobles who would do much to continue their enjoyment of these things forever.

Walking Mountain.notes: Defers to: Mountain (use that entry's statline)

Wyrdbearer.notes: Not so much a creature as a geographical feature, a walking mountain is one of the Carven Peaks that has been so completely imbued with the Pale Emperor's power that it now has a degree of mobility.

Glass Spider.notes: Neither a true spider nor truly glass, this creature is a denizen of cold _arratus_ , having been imported from some alien world as a useful pack predator.

Scorpion Leech.notes: Dog-sized abominations found often in swampy _arratu_ terrain, a scorpion leech is a soft-bodied creature with six chitinous legs, a needle-sharp tail, and an intricate circular maw of rotating teeth.

Screamer Tree.notes: This family of animate flora is found most often in jungle-type _arratus_ , though relatives can be found in the lands of the Verdancy and other places where plants have been warped by sorcery.

Snow Fungus.notes: This fungal life form is found in extremely cold _arratus_ , prospering in conditions that would kill most terrestrial life forms.

Wiggler Dog.notes: The product of some Outsider's spite, these terrestrial dogs were spliced together with a jellyfish-like alien predator.

Antinom.notes: The Antinom is a living curse-weapon devised by some ancient sorcerer-king to bring down the civilizations of his rivals.

Changeling.notes: Once spread among the inhabitants of Tigat in Atba Sim, changelings are a breed of Blighted created by the Tormentors of Vesh to deceive, betray, and immiserate humanity.

Chawi.notes: The Chawi are the unfortunate consequence of a Nakadi plan to create sorcerously-gifted superhumans so as to empower their temple against their rival Word Priests.

Dear Companion.notes: The Chawi are the unfortunate consequence of a Nakadi plan to create sorcerously-gifted superhumans so as to empower their temple against their rival Word Priests.

Flayer.notes: The flayer curse is embedded in the lineage of certain unfortunate baseline bloodlines, but has also been known to afflict certain demihumans, particularly elves.

Ghoul.notes: While these Blighted are sometimes reputed to be undead, a ghoul is actually a baseline or demihuman infected with an unbearable hunger for human flesh.

Giant.notes: Scholars argue over the origins of these unhappy Blighted, but they can now be found in the deep wilderness of both continents.

!Man.notes: Defers to: Same Type of Human (use that entry's statline)

Troll.notes: There are a thousand different kinds of immortality in the Latter Earth, and most of them are little more than lasting damnations.

Cattle of Dis.notes: Some ancient sorcerer wished to devise a breed of cattle that could survive the perils of the open ranges of the Latter Earth.

Flying Jellyfish.notes: Aerial stealth predators, each the size of a bull, flying jellyfish spend daylight hours floating among the clouds.

Kraken Shrimp.notes: A dreaded horror of the coastal seas, the kraken shrimp is a monstrous entity that averages fifty feet from mandibles to tailfin, and twenty in breadth.

Sea Titan.notes: Some scholars claim that these beings are survivors of the sunken kingdom of Llum, while others credit them as native creatures of a former age.

Yuun.notes: Some scholars claim that these beings are survivors of the sunken kingdom of Llum, while others credit them as native creatures of a former age.

Genius Loci.notes: At times, a place of particular natural power or arcane significance will form a Genius Loci, a spirit embodying the nature of the place and the surrounding few miles of land.

Guardian Spirit.notes: Most often bound by ancient sorcerers as protectors of their sanctums and vaults, Guardian Spirits come in numerous shapes and sizes.

Hungry Corpse.notes: The unnatural energies that animate undead are flawed in some cases, sufficient to give them motion but not to give them satiety.

Lich.notes: The dreadful result of deep necromantic lore, a Lich is an undead sorcerer who has prolonged their life through various forbidden and terrible arts.

Skull Knight.notes: Some necromancers or death-cults are not satisfied with creating hosts of shambling, half-witted minions.

Slave Husk.notes: Named for the frequency with which they are enslaved by Necromancers or enthralled by more potent undead, slave husks are wretched men and women who have stirred to an uneasy half-death due to some la

Wraith Lord (atlas).notes: The fearsome princes of the dead, a wraith lord is a powerful ruler who has been animated by skilled death-cultists or an age-old cultural tradition of necromancy.
